subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make only the isolated sandbox `/workspace` writable by default while continuing to keep the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: The requested behavior would restore a useful isolated working area, but current docs/tests encode read-only `none` and the change affects sandbox write authorization.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable none
options.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access, not no sandbox writes, and require a complete mount/bridge/tool/docs/test update that preserves real workspace isolation.

options.title: Keep none read-only
options.body: Leave the current security default in place, update docs/support guidance as needed, and close or reframe the issue as expected behavior.

options.title: Fold into least-privilege bind design
options.body: Defer this exact semantic change and resolve it together with writable custom bind policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable none
recommendation.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access, not no sandbox writes, and require a complete mount/bridge/tool/docs/test update that preserves real workspace isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current sandbox/security history and CODEOWNERS-protected surface point to this account as the best available routing owner for the boundary decision.
